_about: Rejection Rescue playbook: what Apple means by each common rejection, what usually causes it, what to check in the app, how to fix it, and what to say back. Sections are written the way Apple writes them in the App Review Guidelines. Grows from every real rejection the factory sees (Phase 8).

2.1.title: App Completeness (often 'Information Needed')
2.1.means: The reviewer couldn't fully review the app, or needs more information before they can.
causes: a crash or a broken flow on the reviewer's device (often an iPad)
features behind a login with no demo account
missing answers about purpose, audience, setup, outside services or regions
no screen recording on a real device for a new developer account
in-app purchases not submitted with the app
checks: store gate G1 (review notes answer Apple's headings)
rapple-review behavior: cold launch, no crash, iPad launch
store gate A3/A4 (sample data, self-playing tour)
fix: Answer every question Apple asked, under its own heading, in the reply and in App Review Information > Notes
Record the tour on a real phone (one tap) and link it
Make sure sample data reaches every screen with nothing set up
Retest on an iPad simulator

2.3.title: Accurate Metadata
2.3.means: Something in the listing doesn't match the app, or hides what the app does.
causes: description promises a feature the build doesn't have
screenshots or preview show something the app can't do
keywords stuffed with unrelated terms or competitor names
checks: screenshots come from the UI test run of this build
fix: Remove or reword every claim the current build can't show
Regenerate screenshots from this exact build
2.3.reply: Thank you. We've updated the description and screenshots so they show only what this version does: {changes}

2.3.3.title: Screenshots must show the app in use
2.3.3.means: Screenshots can't be only title art, a login screen or a splash screen.
causes: marketing art instead of real screens
a splash or login screen as a screenshot
checks: a human look at every screenshot
fix: Use real screens from the UI test's screenshot run, with at most a short caption above each
2.3.3.reply: Thank you. We've replaced the screenshots with screens of the app in use: {changes}

2.3.10.title: Don't mention other platforms
2.3.10.means: The listing or app names another platform (Android, Google Play) or uses unrelated content.
causes: 'Also on Android' in the description
Android or Play references left in app text
checks: rapple-review static: other platforms named in UI or metadata
fix: Remove every reference to other platforms from the listing, screenshots and app text
2.3.10.reply: Thank you. We've removed references to other platforms from the app and its listing.

2.5.4.title: Background services only for their intended purpose
2.5.4.means: A declared background mode isn't used for what it's meant for.
causes: UIBackgroundModes left on from a template
background audio or location used to keep the app alive
checks: rapple-review static: background modes declared but unused
fix: Remove every background mode the app doesn't need, or explain the feature that needs it in the review notes
2.5.4.reply: Thank you. We've removed the background mode{s} the app doesn't use: {changes}

3.1.1.title: In-App Purchase
3.1.1.means: Digital content or features must be unlocked with Apple's in-app purchase, and the purchases must be submitted with the app.
causes: a link or button to pay on a website for digital content
a third-party payment SDK used for digital unlocks
IAP products not attached to the submission
fix: Route every digital unlock through StoreKit
Remove outside-payment links for digital goods
Attach the in-app purchases to the version before resubmitting
3.1.1.reply: Thank you. Digital features are now unlocked only through in-app purchase, and the purchases are submitted with this version: {changes}

3.1.2.title: Subscriptions
3.1.2.means: The subscription screen or listing is missing required information or doesn't deliver ongoing value.
causes: price, duration or what's included not clear before purchase
no links to Terms of Use (EULA) and the privacy policy
no restore purchases
free-trial terms unclear
fix: Show price, period and what's included before the buy button
Add Terms of Use and privacy policy links on the paywall and in the description
Add Restore Purchases
3.1.2.reply: Thank you. The subscription screen now shows the price, period and what's included before purchase, with links to the Terms of Use and privacy policy, and a Restore Purchases button: {changes}

4.2.title: Minimum Functionality
4.2.means: The app is too limited, or is mainly a website wrapped in an app.
causes: one screen or a single feature
a web view showing a website
content better suited to a website
fix: Explain in the reply what the app does that a website can't (on-device features, offline, notifications, camera)
If it's thin, add the core feature that makes it worth installing before resubmitting
4.2.reply:
Thank you. To clarify what the app does on the device: {answers}

We've also {changes}

4.3.title: Spam
4.3.means: The app looks too similar to other apps, including our own, or to a saturated category.
causes: several apps from one account that share screens or templates
a category with many near-identical apps
fix: Show what's different in function, not looks; consider combining similar apps into one
4.3.reply: Thank you. This app differs from others in the category in what it does: {answers}

4.8.title: Login Services
4.8.means: An app that offers third-party or social login must also offer an equivalent privacy-focused login option.
causes: Google or Facebook login without an equivalent option
fix: Add Sign in with Apple, or another login that meets 4.8's requirements
4.8.reply: Thank you. We've added a login option that meets Guideline 4.8: {changes}

5.1.1.title: Data Collection and Storage
5.1.1.means: Data handling isn't clear, consented or necessary, or a permission's purpose text is missing or vague, or account deletion is missing.
causes: a permission requested at launch instead of in context
vague purpose strings ('We need access')
personal data sent somewhere without saying what, to whom, and asking first
accounts with no in-app deletion (5.1.1(v))
privacy policy that doesn't cover what the app actually does
checks: rapple-review static: purpose strings, privacy manifest, SDKs vs App Privacy answer, accounts
rapple-review behavior: no permission prompt at launch
fix: Ask for each permission only when the person uses the feature that needs it, with a plain purpose string
Before any personal data leaves the phone, say what is sent and to whom, and ask (Allow / Not now)
Add in-app account deletion if there are accounts
Make the privacy policy match the app
5.1.1.reply:
Thank you. Before any personal data leaves the device, the app now shows what will be sent and to whom, and asks for permission first. The privacy policy says the same: {changes}

A recording of this on a physical device: {recording_url}

5.1.2.title: Data Use and Sharing
5.1.2.means: Personal data is shared with a third party (including an AI service) without clear disclosure and permission.
causes: messages or files sent to an AI provider without asking first
analytics or ads SDKs sharing data the App Privacy answer doesn't declare
checks: rapple-review static: outside-service endpoints and SDKs vs App Privacy
fix: Name the service that receives the data, say what is sent, and ask before the first send
Make the App Privacy answers match every SDK
5.1.2.reply: Thank you. The app now names the service that receives the data, says what is sent, and asks before the first send. The App Privacy answers match: {changes}

5.2.5.title: Apple Products
5.2.5.means: Apple's product names are used in a way that's confusing or not allowed.
causes: 'iPhone', 'iPad', 'Siri' or 'Apple Intelligence' in the name or subtitle
Apple product images in screenshots
fix: Remove Apple product names from the name, subtitle and keywords; keep them only where describing compatibility in the description is allowed
5.2.5.reply: Thank you. We've removed Apple product names from the app's name, subtitle and keywords: {changes}
